DESCRIPTION: All tickets in this epic depend on LED-30 (Epic 2). Ordered by value - Reports, Accounts and Home gain most from the freed width, do those three first, per specs/tickets.md 'Suggested build order' #8.

SUMMARY: One set of controls, not two
USER_STORY: As a user on Reports, I want one set of range controls, not a duplicated desktop/mobile pair that can drift.
DESCRIPTION: ReportsPage.tsx [9a]. Range and presets are built twice: a hidden md:flex card pair and a separate md:hidden Select + button, same state, two trees. Also fold the two full-width control cards (Date Range, Saved Presets) into the header row - ~240px of vertical chrome before a single figure.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: One control tree serves both breakpoints; the two full-width control cards are folded into the header row.

USER_STORY: As a user viewing a Reports stat card, I want a comparison to the previous period so the number has a reference point.
DESCRIPTION: ReportsPage.tsx [9a]. $3,812.65 with nothing to judge it against isn't reporting; monthlyData already holds the previous month, so '+11.8% vs Aug' is one subtraction.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Every stat card shows a vs-previous-period comparison derived from existing monthlyData.

USER_STORY: As a desktop user on Reports, I want to see all seven table columns and readably sized charts at 1920, not a column set hidden by an obsolete width cap.
DESCRIPTION: ReportsPage.tsx [9a]. Charts are h-52 at every viewport - let them fill their row and abbreviate y-axis ticks (8k) instead of formatCurrency in a 72px gutter. The table hides Category below sm, Account below md, Balance below lg - and max-w-5xl means Balance is hidden at 1024 even in a 1920 window.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Charts fill their row with abbreviated y-axis ticks; show all seven table columns with a Columns control; selected preset chips no longer use background: GOLD (retired with LED-21, since gold otherwise always means loans).

USER_STORY: As a user re-importing an overlapping statement, I want likely duplicates flagged, not silently written twice.
DESCRIPTION: ImportCSVDialog.tsx. Re-import the same statement, or one overlapping last month by three days, and you get silent duplicates with no way to tell them apart.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Match on date + amount + normalised description before the write; a match defaults to skip (unticked) and names the row it matched.

USER_STORY: As a user importing a CSV, I want most rows pre-categorised from past payee history instead of every row hardcoded to no category.
DESCRIPTION: ImportCSVDialog.tsx. category_id: null is hardcoded for every row and the dialog apologises for it twice.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: A payee -> category memory from past transactions gets most rows right; the rest show 'Choose...' inline.

SUMMARY: Selectable rows, real preview, right account, right currency
USER_STORY: As a user importing a large CSV, I want to review and select rows before committing, and have the import target the right account and currency.
DESCRIPTION: ImportCSVDialog.tsx. parsed.rows maps straight to the insert, so one bad row means cancel, edit the CSV, re-drop. max-w-2xl + PREVIEW_ROW_COUNT = 8 means the user approves 142 transactions having seen six percent of them. setAccountId(accounts[0].id) auto-picks whatever account is first. Preview formats with selectedAccount?.currency ?? 'PHP', so a PHP statement imported into a USD account renders and imports as dollars, unconverted and unwarned. ImportTx allows only income | expense, so a transfer between own accounts imports twice and inflates both totals.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Full, selectable preview (not capped at 8 of 142); explicit account selection with no silent first-account default; currency shown and converted/warned correctly; a transfer kind is supported so it does not import twice.

USER_STORY: As a user viewing Accounts, I want assets and liabilities compared side by side with per-row context, not a stacked list with a summary-only warning.
DESCRIPTION: AccountsPage.tsx [6a]. Assets and Liabilities side by side - that's the comparison the page is about.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: A share bar per asset row; the excluded-currency warning moves onto the row that's excluded (today one amber line under the summary names the currencies, so you can't tell which account was dropped); due dates collect into a 'Coming up' cell instead of scattered chips; liability cards get real actions (Pay card / Repay loan); loan progress gets a meter to match the card utilisation bar.

SUMMARY: Flatten the credit-card monitor and fix its palette
USER_STORY: As a user viewing Home, I want the credit-card monitor to use the app's real palette and a flatter layout, not raw amber/sky colours in four nested boxes.
DESCRIPTION: DashboardCreditCardMonitor [18a]. Nests boxes four deep (card -> bordered inner card -> four border-border/40 rows -> up to two reminder strips) at lg:col-span-2. Its reminder strips are the only place on Home that leaves the app palette - raw amber-500/700 and sky-500/700 where everything else uses INCOME / EXPENSE / GOLD from constants/colors. Utilisation colour is binary (nearLimit ? EXPENSE : INCOME), so 0% and 69% render identically green then snap to red.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Flattened structure; reminder strips use INCOME/EXPENSE/GOLD tokens; utilisation colour is a gradient/scale, not a binary snap.

USER_STORY: As a user on Home at desktop, I want the widget grid to use the freed width without scrolling, and Upcoming Bills to be a compact strip, not a full grid cell.
DESCRIPTION: [18a]. Upcoming Bills is first in DEFAULT_WIDGET_ORDER (correct) but spends a whole grid cell on two rows of text.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Upcoming Bills renders as a strip; three columns at 1920 fit the eight default widgets without scrolling; mobile shows the first four above the fold, user order respected.

USER_STORY: As a mobile or tablet user, I want to view a transaction's detail without being dropped into edit mode.
DESCRIPTION: EntryDetail.tsx (55 lines) [13b]. Renders only at lg: today; below that, tapping a row opens the edit form, so on a phone there is no way to look at a transaction without entering edit mode on it.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Transaction detail renders as its own surface (dialog/sheet) below lg, distinct from the edit form.

USER_STORY: As a user viewing a transaction's detail, I want delete, split, budget impact, tags and receipt visible there, not scattered across a swipe gesture and the edit form only.
DESCRIPTION: EntryDetail.tsx [13b]. One action (onEdit) today: delete is behind a row swipe, and Split has no entry point from the transaction you'd split. Transfers list Account and To account as two unrelated <dl> rows. Add budget impact (this entry's share of the category bar), tags and receipt - all three form fields absent from the detail view. transaction.date prints raw as 2026-09-09.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Delete and Split actions present; transfers render as from -> to; budget impact, tags and receipt shown; date is formatted, not raw ISO.

USER_STORY: As a user splitting a transaction, I want the unassigned remainder offered as one tap, rows instead of stacked cards, and a clear warning that splitting is irreversible.
DESCRIPTION: SplitTransactionDialog.tsx [13a]. addLine already seeds the new line with diff, but only if the user thinks to press Add line. Lines are stacked ~130px cards in a max-w-xl dialog, so three splits need scrolling. '$X over budget' is the wrong phrase - this is over-allocation of one transaction and has nothing to do with Budgets. Splitting deletes the original and writes N new rows, irreversibly, and the dialog never says so. Disabled Split has three causes (unbalanced / blank description / zero amount) and one silent state.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: '$9.40 unassigned -> Add as a line' surfaced directly; lines render as rows, not cards; over-allocation copy no longer references Budgets; the dialog states the delete-and-rewrite is irreversible; each disabled-Split cause is shown distinctly.

USER_STORY: As a user whose tracked loan purchases don't add up to the account balance, I want to be warned every time it happens, not only when the tracker is empty.
DESCRIPTION: LoanPurchaseTracker.tsx [21a, 14a]. The warning renders only when purchases.length === 0, inside the create modal - shown once, then never again. But getLoanAmountOwed(account) and the sum of purchases can drift apart at any time, and the gap is debt with no schedule and no deadline.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: The reconciliation warning appears on the tracker whenever the two figures disagree, not only on an empty purchase list.

SUMMARY: Schedule you can scan and pay
USER_STORY: As a user viewing a loan's payment schedule, I want a scrolling list with the next payment pinned and a way to pay it, not a 4-row paginated list collapsed by default.
DESCRIPTION: LoanPurchaseTracker.tsx [21a, 14a]. DEADLINES_PAGE_SIZE = 4 with prev/next and every row collapsed by default (expandedDeadline starts null). The tracker computes the next deadline and its per-purchase split and offers no way to pay it. opening_installments_paid renders an identical progress bar to money actually repaid. Recent Payment Splits drops the installment number.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Scrolling list replaces pagination; next payment pinned and expanded with a launch-loan-repayment-form-prefilled action; imported-as-paid installments get a visually distinct progress segment from actually-repaid ones; installment number shown in Recent Payment Splits.

USER_STORY: As a user taking out a loan purchase, I want to see the total interest and the schedule preview before I commit, not just the total payable.
DESCRIPTION: LoanPurchaseForm.tsx [14a]. totalPayable is shown; interest (totalPayable - principal) never is - at 1.25% flat over 24 months that's $720 on $2,400, 30% over sticker. Term and rate are on different steps.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Interest amount named alongside totalPayable; term and rate visible together; schedule preview (first date, last date, true final installment); 'Already Paid' count and the adjacent currency summary are both labelled; shows the effect on the parent loan (outstanding after, new monthly obligation).

SUMMARY: Type grid, liability sign, period fields
USER_STORY: As a user creating or editing an account, I want the type choice, the liability sign, and the loan schedule fields to be visible and explained up front, not discovered on submit.
DESCRIPTION: Account form [19a]. Type becomes a visible 8-cell grid (all eight types have icons in ACCOUNT_ICONS) since the choice changes which fields appear. normalizeLiabilityBalanceForStorage flips the sign the user types - getting it backwards silently inverts net worth. superRefine has four branches across seven periods in LOAN_PAY_PERIOD_LABELS, all discovered on submit today.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: 8-cell type grid; liability sign explained where it's entered; preview day numbers (statement_day + due_day = days to pay); each loan period's required control shown live, not on submit; available credit computed live (credit_limit + balance); nullable fields marked optional with what's lost by skipping them stated.

USER_STORY: As a user viewing Budgets & Goals, I want them as separate segmented views since the header period applies to budgets, not goals, and I want goals to state plainly that they are manually tracked.
DESCRIPTION: BudgetsPage.tsx [4b, 23a].
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Budgets and Goals split into segmented views; over-budget rows cap the bar at 100% and carry the true percentage in the number; the budget cycle (getBudgetCycleRange) dates are shown in the form; goals derive and display the monthly contribution needed from target + saved + date; goals state plainly they are manual (no account link, hand-edited current_amount, transfers don't move the goal).

SUMMARY: Budget form shows the real allowance
USER_STORY: As a user editing a budget, I want to see how rollover and the deficit setting change my effective limit, not just the number I typed.
DESCRIPTION: BudgetForm [23a, 28a]. Surface the already-computed rollover_amount as base limit -> carried in -> effective, and which deficit behaviour is active.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Budget form shows base limit -> carried in -> effective, and names the active deficit behaviour.

USER_STORY: As a user reading any legal page, I want one consistent layout, and no decorative clutter on Data Deletion.
DESCRIPTION: Legal pages [24a]. All three rebuild the same skeleton (back links, icon, title, last-updated, sections, separators, footer) in their own file. Red (--expense) currently colours both section headings, all four step numbers and the summary box.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Single <LegalPage> layout serves all three documents; the atmospheric layer (gradient, dot grid, two bleed circles) is deleted from DataDeletionPage; red is reserved for step 04 and the no-grace-period warning; all three pages cross-link.

SUMMARY: CSV export beside the deletion instructions
USER_STORY: As a user about to delete my data, I want to export it first from the same page.
DESCRIPTION: Data deletion page [24a]. Reports already has the exporter.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: CSV export control present on the data-deletion page, reusing the existing Reports exporter.

USER_STORY: As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want the active nav destination announced and the seven top-bar tabs reachable as one tab stop, plus a way to skip straight to content.
DESCRIPTION: [27a]. aria-current has zero occurrences in the codebase - Sidebar.tsx and BottomNav.tsx mark the active destination by background tint alone. Blocking for 2B, which puts seven tabs where the rail was.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: aria-current on the active nav destination; seven tabs are one tab stop via roving tabIndex (active 0, others -1, arrows move) + role='tablist'; one <a href='#main'> skip link, visible on focus.

USER_STORY: As a keyboard user opening and closing a dialog or sheet, I want focus to land on the heading, then return to the trigger on close.
DESCRIPTION: [27a]. Matters most for 5a -> form and 5b picker -> form.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: On open, focus moves to the heading, not the first field; on close, focus returns to the trigger.

USER_STORY: As a user hitting a data error, I want a plain-language sentence, not a raw error.message string.
DESCRIPTION: ~20 sites: useAccounts (:38, :90, :105, :124, :162), useLoanPurchases (:53, :71, :100, :125, :139), useExchangeRates (:116, :154, :204), useBudgets (:59, :88), useCategories (:36, :106), useSubcategories:106, useTransactions:87, useSavingsGoals:40, SettingsPage:274 [26a] spec Section5.13.1 area.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: The codes that actually occur (unique violation, RLS denial, connection failure) map to plain sentences; the raw text stays collapsed for support.

USER_STORY: As a user hitting a partial failure or wanting to undo an action, I want one consistent notification surface with an appropriate severity, not a single undo-toast used by two pages and nothing else.
DESCRIPTION: ui/undo-toast.tsx, ui/error-boundary.tsx:32, BudgetsPage.tsx:641 [26a]. ui/undo-toast.tsx is used only by TransactionsPage and AccountTransactionsPage for undo-delete. ui/error-boundary.tsx:32 renders 'Something went wrong.' with no retry. Off-system colours in BudgetsPage.tsx:641 (bg-yellow-500 / bg-emerald-500 where GOLD / INCOME exist).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: One notification surface with three severities: success + undo, failure + retry, partial failure + fix; error boundary scoped to the failed section with a stated safe-state and recovery action; BudgetsPage uses GOLD/INCOME tokens instead of raw Tailwind colours.

USER_STORY: As a user waiting for content to load, I want a skeleton shaped like the real content, not a generic pulse block.
DESCRIPTION: ReportsPage.tsx (:948, :1186, :1236, :1285) [25a]. Four hand-rolled animate-pulse blocks despite the same file importing and correctly using Skeleton six other times. Skeleton hard-codes rounded-md while call sites override with several different radii.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Four hand-rolled pulses replaced with Skeleton; row grid/icon tile/dividers stay real, only text runs grey out (no load-time layout shift); Skeleton's default radius decided/reconciled with card radius; spinner-for-user-triggered-action vs skeleton-for-content-arriving rule applied consistently.

USER_STORY: As a user stepping the month cycle, I want the previous cycle's data to stay visible while the next loads, not a full-page skeleton flash.
DESCRIPTION: Month cycle stepping, AppLayout shell [25a, 2B]. Stepping the month cycle swaps content for skeletons despite data being on screen. The shell never loads: nav, period stepper, title and primary action depend on no query and should be interactive from the first frame.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Previous cycle stays visible at reduced opacity with a progress rule and a named loading target, preserving scroll position; the shell (nav, stepper, title, primary action) is interactive from the first frame with no skeleton.

SUMMARY: Login says what the product is
USER_STORY: As a new visitor to the login page, I want to know what Ledger does before I'm asked to sign in.
DESCRIPTION: Login page [11a]. The page never says what Ledger does: a stranger sees a wordmark, a five-word tagline and a Google button. max-w-100 centres a phone-width column on a 1920 display. error_description prints raw.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: A two-panel layout at 1920 that explains the product; OAuth error text is translated to plain language, not printed raw.

USER_STORY: As a user reviewing the 13th Month estimate, I want it stated once, records visible by default, and salary-only selection to be one click.
DESCRIPTION: ThirteenthMonthPage.tsx [15a]. Beyond LED-06: the estimate is printed three times on one page; months start collapsed so the include/exclude checkbox sits on a closed row.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Estimate shown once; months expanded by default; 'auto-select salary only' control added.

USER_STORY: As a user on an account detail page, I want a breadcrumb and the key figures in one band, with room for payment and category breakdown alongside.
DESCRIPTION: Account detail [4a].
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Breadcrumb replaces the back-chevron; balance / limit / statement / due share one ruled band; right pane carries payment + category breakdown.

USER_STORY: As a desktop user on Activity, I want the entry-detail pane to have a permanent home at 1920 without squeezing the transaction list.
DESCRIPTION: Activity [3a]. The freed width finally gives the entry-detail pane a home without squeezing the list.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: Entry-detail pane has a dedicated home at 1920; list stays full width at smaller sizes.

SUMMARY: Mobile add transaction uses the full form
USER_STORY: As a mobile user adding a transaction, I want the same form as on tablet and desktop, not a calculator keypad.
DESCRIPTION: AppLayout.tsx, QuickEntry.tsx, src/lib/entryAmount.ts [4c] add-transaction-spec Section4. Below the mobile breakpoint AppLayout renders QuickEntry: a 12-key keypad driven by editEntryAmount with Payee, Note, tags and recurring behind a More details disclosure, while tablet and desktop render TransactionForm. QuickEntry already falls back to TransactionForm for loan and card payments, so two entry forms exist for one entity. Decision (2026-09-24): replace QuickEntry with TransactionForm on mobile rather than keep it with a numeric field. The 4c design caption still describes the keypad; the spec and this decision supersede it.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: The mobile add sheet renders TransactionForm with the same props as desktop (entryKind, locked card and loan accounts); the amount is a numeric field that raises the OS keyboard (inputMode="decimal"); no keypad renders at any size; QuickEntry.tsx and entryAmount.ts are deleted with no remaining imports and tests/redesign.mjs no longer exercises keypad editing; every kind (expense, income, transfer, loan repayment, card payment) saves from the mobile sheet; the sheet has a sticky save and fits 390 x 844 without the page scrolling behind it.
